planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; cut back hard in late winter to renew wood and keep the rounded habit dense and floriferous.

directions: Asian Moon is a triploid hybrid butterfly bush bred for sterility, producing light purple flower spikes with distinctive orange throats from June into fall without setting the viable seed that has made some older Buddleja davidii cultivars invasive in parts of the country. Because it channels no energy into seed production, it reblooms nearly continuously on new growth, drawing heavy butterfly and hummingbird traffic through the whole season. It grows into a full-size rounded shrub, larger than dwarf series selections like Blue Chip or Ice Chip, so give it room in a border or as an informal hedge. It tolerates heat and drought once established and benefits from an annual hard cutback in late winter to encourage vigorous, compact new growth.
